note: Curves P-256, P-384 and P-521; outputs PEM (the public key as PUBLIC KEY, a blank line, then the PKCS #8 PRIVATE KEY, byte for byte what OpenSSL writes), DER (CyberChef's name for the private scalar alone as hex) and JWK ({"keys": [private, public]}, 4 spaces of indent, with key_ops and kid). The private scalar is made from random:bytes-of (FIPS 186-5 appendix A.2: seed mod (n - 1) + 1) instead of the jsrsasign generator, so the op has the +random effect. Layout, option order and defaults were compared with the CyberChef 11.5.0 module source. The input is ignored, as in CyberChef.

PEM private keys, SEC1 (EC PRIVATE KEY) or PKCS #8 (PRIVATE KEY), on P-256, P-384, P-521 and also secp256k1; digests sha256, sha384, sha512, sha1 and md5 (a choice named sha256 and so on); output formats asn1-hex, p1363-hex, jws and raw-json. The signature is deterministic (RFC 6979, which two independent implementations agree on); CyberChef's jsrsasign uses a random k, so the same key and message give a different signature there on every call and the same one here. Every ECDSA verifier accepts both. The input bytes are hashed as bytes (CyberChef decodes them as UTF-8 text first). raw-json writes r and s as the hex of their DER INTEGER content, as jsrsasign does (with a leading 00 when the top bit is set). A public key, an RSA or Ed25519 key, an encrypted key and explicit curve parameters are E_COERCE; no key is E_RANGE.

The signature is the input, in the format of the input-format parameter or auto (JSON object, then hex that is DER if it starts 30 and parses, else P1363, then URL-safe Base64 as JWS); the message is a parameter read as UTF-8 text, hex, Base64 or Latin-1 (CyberChef: Raw, Hex, Base64; Raw is UTF-8 here, Latin-1 is added). Answers Verified OK or Verification Failure, CyberChef's texts; a signature of either half of s and of any k is accepted. A private key where a public key is wanted, a key that is not on its curve, and a signature that cannot be read are E_COERCE (CyberChef throws for the first and falls back to an error for the last), no key is E_RANGE. A signature value too wide for the curve, zero, or at least the order is a failure.

Between asn1-hex, p1363-hex, jws (URL-safe Base64 of r || s) and raw-json ({"r":"hex","s":"hex"}), with auto detection of the input as in ECDSA Verify (white space around the text is ignored). The curve is unknown, so P1363 and JWS are written at the smallest of 32, 48 and 66 bytes that holds r and s (CyberChef pads to a multiple of 16 bytes by a rule that, as far as the source shows, cannot write a P-521 signature; not run). A value over 66 bytes cannot be written as P1363 or JWS (E_COERCE) but converts to DER and JSON. JSON r and s are read as unsigned hex, with or without a leading 00; a missing, empty or non-hex value is E_COERCE with CyberChef's message.

GB/T 32918.4 on sm2p256v1, with the public key as its two 32-byte coordinates in hex, and the order C1C3C2 or C1C2C3. As CyberChef writes it: the output is hex text, C1 is x || y (64 bytes, no 04 byte). k is random from random:bytes-of (the op has the +random effect), with the standard's retry when the key stream is all zero. The layout is from CyberChef 11.5.0's source (read, not run); the encryption was checked against the GB/T 32918.5-2017 annex example (fixed k) and OpenSSL decrypts it.

The input is the ciphertext as hex text (white space ignored, either case; CyberChef needs lower case to compare C3), the private key 32 bytes as hex. C1 may be x || y or have the 04 byte (found by checking that the point is on the curve), so ciphertexts of other SM2 libraries decrypt; OpenSSL's are read after regrouping its DER. A wrong key, order or damaged data fails the C3 check: E_COERCE (CyberChef: Decryption Error -- Computed Hashes Do Not Match). The result is bytes.

CyberChef's GOST Sign is not a public key signature: it is the MAC mode of the GOST block ciphers. Forge offers the GOST 28147-89 MAC (the IMIT of RFC 5830 section 8) with CyberChef's key, IV, S-box and MAC length (8 to 64 bits, default 32); the S-boxes are those of gost28147 (E-TEST, E-A, E-B, E-C, E-D, E-Z, D-TEST, D-A; not E-SC and D-SC), and Magma and Kuznyechik (the 2015 algorithms) are not offered. The input and output types of CyberChef (Raw or Hex) are not parameters: the input is bytes and the MAC is bytes, chain From Hex and To Hex. The GOST R 34.10-2012 public key signature that the name suggests is the separate gost3410:sign (an addition, no CyberChef row). The S-box tables are shared with gost28147 (no private copy).

The check of the MAC of GOST Sign, for the GOST 28147-89 algorithm only (see GOST Sign for what is not offered). The MAC is a parameter (hex by default, 1 to 8 bytes; its length decides how many bits are compared, as in CyberChef); the answers are The signature matches and The signature does not match, CyberChef's texts. The S-box tables are shared with gost28147 (no private copy).
